newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico starts coffee campaign to fight berry borer.
newsitem.headline: Mexico starts coffee campaign to fight berry borer.

text.p: Mexico published a campaign outline Wednesday that will bid to fight the infamous berry borer that blights coffee production.

The campaign, detailed in a 24-page document published in the government's Official Gazette, sets down obligatory phytosanitary rules in law in the battle against the berry borer, often known as by its Spanish name - broca.
Mexico, along with most coffee producing nations, is troubled by the berry borer, a beetle that eats part of the coffee beans inside the cherries, damaging coffee quality and affecting weight.

"This official standard establishes the obligatory rules that will have to be fulfilled to confine, control, and in the future, erradicate the points of infestation of broca, as well as avoid its spreading to coffee zones free of the plague," the official gazette said.
Mexico's Agriculture Ministry has been working with the Mexican Coffee Council to put in place the legal framework for the campaign for 17 months.
Broca, which originated from Africa, was first spotted in Guatemala in 1971 and seven years later was found in Mixcum, Chiapas, Mexico's southern state that borders Guatemala.

The campaign is applicable to all coffee types, by-products and plants, to coffee growing zones, production mills and warehouses and even covers transport means and packaging, from containers to bags.

Among the most important aspects of the campaign are the quarantine rules, restricting the movement of coffee with the aim of preventing or at least slowing down the introduction of broca where it is not known to exist.
One of the means to be used to control broca will be attempts to sterilize beetles by chemicals, using pesticides, insecticides and fungicides or natural means, it added.
Seven producing states were mentioned as having quarantined zones.
Areas that put an end to broca outbreaks will be declared berry borer free and notices will be published in the Official Gazette.
Certification groups will also be established which will be empowered to evaluate the carrying out of the standards and lawe, expedite phytosanitary permits and follow up certifications.
